name: Fenix PD36R Pro Rechargeable Flashlight
summary: A handheld 21700-powered emergency light with USB-C charging and five brightness levels. Its 2,800-lumen Turbo is a peak setting with heat-driven stepdown; the 42-hour figure belongs to Eco.
description: The PD36R Pro is for someone who needs a directional handheld beam for checking a path, an electrical panel area or outdoor surroundings during an outage. Choose a sustainable lower mode for routine work and reserve Turbo for brief inspection. The dual tail switches favour quick control, but a handheld beam occupies one hand: compare the existing HM50R V2.0 headlamp for hands-free tasks or CL26R Pro lantern for area lighting. This is specifically the PD36R Pro, not the original PD36R, V2.0, TAC or ACE. Plan charging before an outage and retain a separate light in case the battery is depleted or misplaced. The owner’s diagonal illustration includes a holster and a small plastic case, but neither the picture nor the manufacturer’s separate package list verifies what the selected Amazon seller supplies.

specs.label: Exact model
specs.value: PD36R Pro; five steady brightness levels plus strobe

specs.label: Manufacturer modes
specs.value: Turbo 2,800 lm; High 1,000 lm; Medium 350 lm; Low 150 lm; Eco 30 lm

specs.label: Conditional runtime
specs.value: Eco 30 lm: up to 42 h. Turbo total 3 h 30 min includes reduced output after stepdown; not constant 2,800 lm.

specs.label: Beam distance
specs.value: Up to 380 m manufacturer FL1 beam-distance figure; not a guaranteed identification distance

specs.label: Power / recharge
specs.value: One compatible 21700 Li-ion battery; documented ARB-L21-5000 5,000 mAh; USB-C charging

specs.label: Construction
specs.value: A6061-T6 aluminium; manufacturer IP68 to 2 m and 1 m impact rating

specs.label: Size / weight
specs.value: 145.8 mm length; 26.5 mm head; 169 g including battery

pros: A defined set of brightness levels lets the user choose between short inspection and longer lower-output lighting.
USB-C charging can fit an existing outage charging plan when the power source meets the instructions.
Directional handheld lighting complements the different roles of a headlamp and lantern.
cons: Turbo rapidly produces heat and steps down; the total quoted runtime must not be read as sustained maximum output.
This light requires the correct 21700 Li-ion cell; AA and AAA rechargeables are not substitutes.
A narrow handheld beam is less convenient for hands-free work or shared room illumination; retail accessories remain unverified.
useCases: Households preparing a portable inspection light and a separate reserve before a power outage.
Outdoor users checking a path from a safe position, with mode selection practised before darkness.
Buyers comparing a flashlight with the HM50R V2.0 headlamp and CL26R Pro lantern for different lighting tasks.

safetyNotes: Keep the beam out of eyes. High output creates heat; keep the light clear of combustible material and prevent accidental activation during storage according to the manual.
Use only a compatible battery and charging supply. Fenix specifically excludes ARB-L21-6000 and ARB-L21-6000B from this model; do not assume every 21700 fits.
Do not charge damaged cells or wet equipment. Follow the delivered manual for polarity, charging, seal maintenance and storage.
Maximum brightness, runtime, beam distance, impact and water figures are conditional manufacturer tests, not independent measurements or guarantees for a worn unit.
